headline: Funding flows. Satellites launch. Defense budgets swell.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and strategic developments in the space sector.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid co-orbital buzz
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190M Series C, bringing its valuation to $1.6B. This funding underscores the growing interest in co-orbital security as the DoD pushes for enhanced space domain awareness. With the defense sector's appetite for such capabilities, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on government contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a crowded space, cash is king, and True Anomaly's funding suggests that defense budgets are prioritizing space security more than ever.

stories.head: Blue Origin aims for New Glenn liftoff by year-end
stories.body: Blue Origin has announced plans to resume New Glenn launches by the end of the year, following damage assessments that revealed less severe issues than anticipated. This comes after a prolonged lull in their launch schedule, raising questions about their operational reliability.
stories.soWhat: If Blue Origin can pull off this timeline, it might just restore some investor confidence—but that's a big if in the world of launch schedules.

stories.head: Muon Space unveils ambitious satellite data center plan
stories.body: Muon Space has revealed a Starship-class satellite platform aimed at establishing orbital data centers, with a target launch in 2028. The company is betting that housing data centers in space will be a lucrative market, tapping into the growing need for cloud services.
stories.soWhat: If Muon can make this work, they might just redefine where data lives—but launching a satellite is one thing; making it profitable is another.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on GPS alternatives
watchlist.body: With Murata exploring Xona's satellite timing service, GPS backup solutions may gain traction, impacting traditional navigation systems.

watchlist.title: European space capabilities under scrutiny
watchlist.body: As Europe ramps up defense spending, the lack of investment in space capabilities could become a critical oversight.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: With a $480M extension on the TITAN ground station program, Palantir's dominance in government contracts seems solidified, warranting close observation.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic test delays persist
watchlist.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could signal deeper issues in defense tech timelines, affecting related contracts.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
